the tertiary base pairs G1401:C1498, C1498:G1496, G1501:C1496, and C1497:G1498 exist in the 16S rRNA and are important for the binding of the A- and P-tRNA sites.
the tertiary base pairs C1496:G1405, G1497:C1404, and C1403:1498 are important for the functional integrity of the decoding center in the ribosome.

mutations of C1404 and G1405, which are located in the 5'-end of the decoding region of 16S RNA, and of C1496 and G1497, located in the 3'-end of this region, affect the binding of aminoacyl-tRNA and fMet-tRNA at both A and p sites, and that these effects are reversed by restoring the original base pairs in the reverse orientation.

the tertiary structure of the 16S rRNA of the 30S subunit and its functional implications.
the tertiary structure of the small subunit of the ribosome and its functional implications.
the tertiary structure of the small ribosomal subunit, and its functional importance.

the tertiary base pairs G1401:1501, C1404:1497, and G1405:1496, which are formed between two universally present and sequence-conserved single stranded regions in the 16S rRNA, are functionally important and exist in vivo.
the tertiary base pairs C1496:G1405, C1404:1497, and G1405:1496 are essential for A-site function and C1496:1405 and C1496:C1497 for P-site function.

the tertiary base pairs G1401:C1497, C1404:U1498, and G1405:U1497 are functionally important, that the base pairs C1403:U1498 and C1496:U1497 can form but are not functionally important, and that the base pair C1496:G1497 is functionally important.

there are two tertiary helices, one on the 16S RNA side, one on the P site side, that together make up a 3D structure that is critical for the function of the A and P sites in translation.
